name: Mobilise App Lab Limited

persistent_weak_CAP_CASH_ceiling_assessm.reason: CAP 6 and CASH 6: no persistent value destruction or poor cash realization finding; retain full diagnostic range if missing values later arise, rather than fabricating a point.

ranking_eligibility.reason: G2 centralfinancial basis/perimeterconcerns; scoresare diagnostic only

gates.name: Integrity and minority protection
gates.reason: Related-party guarantee, ownership labeling and reporting controls need clarification. No substantiated severe diversion or misconduct found; no governance override.
gates.resolution: Explain partnership interests, commercial terms, guarantees and sustain documented controls.

gates.name: Financial reliability
gates.reason: FY26 software opens at ₹2.5004 crore versus the IPO-restated ₹3.5821 crore, without a disclosed carry-forward bridge; FY25 equity differs by ₹1.1086 crore. The 98% partnership interest also has conflicting investment and ownership descriptions. These are unresolved analytical reliability concerns, not a fraud conclusion. The IPO/CFO reclassification is resolved and is not the reason for this hold.
gates.resolution: Obtain a company/auditor bridge from FY25 IPO-restated assets and equity to the FY26 statutory opening, including software costs and depreciation. Explain the MobiliseIE consideration, profit share, ownership and any disposal. Reassess materiality and reliance after that reconciliation.

gates.name: Funding and survival
gates.reason: Published cash and eligible IPO resources fund the base assumptions, with minimal debt. No material historical default was identified. Stricter working-capital or program-overlap stresses fail, but those are scenarios, not observed distress.
gates.resolution: Reconcile actual September 2026 deployment and recurring costs. Demonstrate adequate unrestricted cash after taxes, program spending and the chosen operating reserve.

gates.name: Tradability
gates.reason: Security active SM but whole-lot capacity sparse; 20/60 day issuer-row coverage 8/36. Dated surveillance circular not retrieved; no executable bid/offer confirmation.
gates.resolution: Recheck official series/band/surveillance and executable whole-lot depth; no market-order assumption.

factor_audit.name: Governance and stewardship
material_facts: Full FY26 audit/IFC/CARO is clean on its stated tests, but prior audit-trail absence and reporting corrections show weak earlier controls.
Director guarantee 0.7031 crore and compensation/rent/manpower transactions are material relative to 5.5922 crore PAT; contradictory 98% ownership labels remain.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: IPO premium is now correctly classified; director compensation declined, guarantee exposure declined from 1.0118 crore.
factor_audit.rationale: Material disclosure and minority-protection concerns merit 4, not a finding of diversion and not the≤3 governance override.

uncertainty.resolution: Reconcile software/perimeter, document related-party terms and sustain clean controls.

factor_audit.name: Competitive advantage
material_facts: ERP integration, payroll rules and installed workflows can create switching friction.
Largest customer 75.07% of FY25 revenue and no verified cohort retention/pricing data prevent calling that friction a durable bargaining advantage.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Repeat customer 92.94% FY25 and company’s long operating history are genuine relationship evidence.
factor_audit.rationale: Useful contestable niche capability. Azure hosting, AI plans and certifications do not establish a proprietary platform/network moat.

factor_audit.name: Demonstrated revenue growth
material_facts: Three-year reported software-services CAGR 38.45% uses four observations; five-year mixed-basis diagnostic 51.95% is disclosed.
FY2613.90% growth and two halves slowing 27.30% to 4.49% justify net−1 from 9.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Q4 revenue−4.08%; FY25 top-customer concentration makes persistence uncertain.
factor_audit.rationale: Base score 9, net trajectory−1, medium/short-comparable-history ceiling 8. No second small-base penalty; no TAM points. No material acquired issuer revenue identified, but organic growth is not separately certified.

factor_audit.name: Growth runway and demand durability
material_facts: Multiple live product families provide cross-sell and adjacent use cases.
IPO resources enable hiring/marketing, but customer concentration and absent retention data constrain accessible runway.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Product mix outside HRevO is material and less concentrated mix in 9 M 26 is encouraging.
factor_audit.rationale: Demand for payroll/ERP is durable; company-specific capture is not yet demonstrated through a cycle.

factor_audit.name: Attributable incremental returns
material_facts: Restated FY23–25 incremental NOPAT/IC proxy 79.78% is reconciled to actual reinvestment and exceeds a 14–20% nominal INR cost-of-capital range.
FY26 all-development-expensed EBIT 2.2662 crore is below FY25 restated 4.2802, while current opening software basis differs materially.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Historical cumulative FCF 4.2101 crore supports genuine capital efficiency; no mandatory private customer cohort is required to recognize that.
factor_audit.rationale: Mixed rather than unknown or exceptional: strong early organic capital efficiency, but short window, margin leverage, concentration and recent heavier development limit attribution and persistence. Current 3/5 year comparable IC proxy remains NS.

factor_audit.name: Operating cash realization
material_facts: Comparable restated 3-year CFO/PAT 1.0165 x is sound, with positive FCF.
FY26 CFO/PAT 0.9407 x and almost all receivables under 6 months are supportive, but collections benefited from earlier releases and capex now exceeds CFO.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Negative FY26 FCF is predominantly reinvestment, not evidence that CFO itself is negative; IPO financing is removed from CFO.
factor_audit.rationale: Adequate/mixed operating realization. No persistent-CASH≤3 finding, so no GQS 5 ceiling. Software reinvestment affects CAP/EARN and FCF separately.

factor_audit.name: Funding resilience
material_facts: Debt 0.0908 crore is small and 19.3807 crore cash provides substantial eligible project funding.
Most cash 17.13 crore is earmarked; 95 ONWC days or zero overlap with baseline spending breaks reserve assumptions.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Base and bull cash paths are funded, including pre-entry obligations; no reported default.
factor_audit.rationale: Manageable base case but meaningful linked-stress sensitivity, not a blanket funding hold for lack of daily bank statements.

factor_audit.name: Execution and adaptation
material_facts: Sales have scaled across product families and IPO listing/resources were completed.
March 2026 object spend was zero against a ₹1.2075 crore plan; July reply fixed XBRL formatting but the current software/perimeter bridge is still absent.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: The late-February IPO left little time before March year-end and the monitor reported no deviation; zero March spend is not a proven failed project.
factor_audit.rationale: Mixed delivery, short listed history and unmeasured FY27 conversion prevent a strong score.

factor_audit.name: Quality of profit growth
material_facts: Reported FY26 PAT 5.5922 crore is up 15.99% on statutory FY25, but writebacks/prior income and lower director pay helped.
Normalized operating PAT 5.1421 crore and current-share EPS 5.41 are less impressive; fully expensed development EBIT falls.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Normalized operating EBIT remains positive and large, not solely interest or one-off income.
factor_audit.rationale: Real operating profit but capitalization, regime changes and IPO share expansion weaken recurring per-share growth.

factor_audit.name: Expected shareholder return
material_facts: Dated price 101.75 is verified.
Funded conditional base/bull returns diverge widely with program overlap, margin and development-tax assumptions.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Bull case can exceed 15% with 30% growth and material economic-margin improvement.
factor_audit.rationale: G2 holdandunverifiedbudgetoverlapmakeapointreturnratingunreliable. Conditional returns are not ordinary expected returns.

factor_audit.name: Downside and permanent-loss protection
material_facts: Full customer loss and linked cost/working-capital stress break cash floors.
Earmarked cash and software assets do not provide already saleable liquidation protection.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Low reported debt and base funding give a meaningful cushion.
factor_audit.rationale: No single probability-weighted impairment estimate without a cleared financial basis and contract/cost information.

factor_audit.name: Price-implied expectations
material_facts: Finite funded reverse case can be computed with explicit software cash cost and funding constraints.
Required growth is far above latest 13.90%, and terminal multiples have no independent market calibration here.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Early historical growth was above 30%; required scaling is not mathematically impossible.
factor_audit.rationale: Reverse calculation is a research test, not validated price-implied quality while G2 remains open.

factor_audit.name: Liquidity and implementability
material_facts: A 1600-share lot costs ₹162800; reference ₹500000 position needs 3 lots below budget.
Only one observed 20-session row allows one whole lot at 5% participation; missing rows cannot be called zero.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: 19 October did trade 51200 shares; stock is not shown as suspended in the dated master.
factor_audit.rationale: Observed lot capacity is weak and series changed ST to SM.3 reflects actual execution constraints, not an assertion that all silent days had zero volume.

sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text:
Hold — unresolved. Mobilise App Lab is a real, profitable enterprise-software and services business, not merely a technology label. Its earlier cash generation and capital efficiency deserve credit. The current evidence nevertheless does not establish a durable, broadly diversified subscription compounder, and the quoted valuation is less inexpensive after charging software development and preserving the IPO spending commitments.

Business Quality is 5.5 /10 (unrounded 5.46); Growth Quality is 6.5 (unrounded 6.45); Investment Attractiveness is NS. All ranking eligibility is withheld while the material financial-basis bridge remains unresolved. This is a research hold, not an allegation of fraud or an observed funding default.

At the verified 19 October 2026 close of ₹101.75, market capitalization is ₹96.7846 crore. The approximately 17.31 x reported earnings multiple rises to 18.82 x normalized operating earnings and roughly 57.07 x the deliberately conservative fully-expensed-development NOPAT proxy. These are different earnings lenses, not interchangeable peer P/Es. The funded base cash-cost case returns -8.93% annually over the exact October 2026–October 2031 horizon, while the bull reaches 31.08%. The bear is not financeable under its assumptions and has no non-rescue return. Do not average these into a target.

The decisive questions are customer concentration, how much development is genuinely growth investment versus maintenance, and whether the IPO-funded staffing/cloud budget creates incremental recurring profit. No purchase or sale is being proposed.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
Issuer: Mobilise App Lab Limited; NSE Emerge symbol MOBILISE; ISIN INE1YNB01019; CIN L62012HR2023PLC113349. The business began as Mobilise App Lab LLP in 2013, converted to a private company in July 2023 and public company in April 2025. It listed 2 March 2026. Research information cutoff 20 October 2026; market reference 19 October; retrieval 22 October. Later retrieval is not treated as permission to incorporate post-cutoff events.

The full FY2026 statutory report, CARO, IFC and Rule 11 audit-trail observations were inspected, alongside the FY2025 report, final prospectus, corrected-format exchange response, monitoring report and older LLP scans. Confidence is high on exact identity, the dated market row, disclosed product pricing, concentration and the FY2026 reported balance sheet. It is medium on economic earnings, organic continuity and funding assumptions, and low on contract-level retention and the missing current capital/perimeter bridge.

G1 is Conditional, G2 Hold — unresolved, G3 Conditional and G4 Conditional. A clean auditor opinion is meaningful counterevidence but not a substitute for reconciling apparently different accounting populations. G2 is narrowly tied to software carrying values and ownership accounting. The tiny residual after reconciling FY2025 bank deposits, and the corrected IPO/CFO classification, are not used to inflate that concern. The standalone partnership amounts are small in absolute size, so that issue alone would not justify a group-wide distress conclusion.

This analysis applies a nominal INR 15% pre-tax shareholder hurdle, with 12% and 18% sensitivities, and an illustrative ₹500000 position. No user risk tolerance, actual portfolio or cost basis is assumed. Tax in company cash flows is separate from the investor’s taxes.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
The 13 factor register retains two material facts, a contrary fact, evidence references and confidence for each factor. Scores measure different questions: GOV 4, MOAT 5, REV 8, DUR 5, CAP 6, CASH 6, BAL 6, EXEC 5, EARN 5, R NS, D NS, P NS and L 3. An unresolved factor is never assigned a neutral 5.

BQS weights are 20% GOV, 20% MOAT, 12% REV, 10% DUR, 12% CAP, 10% CASH, 8% BAL and 8% EXEC. GQS weights are 40% REV, 20% DUR, 15% EARN, 15% CAP and 10% CASH. Exact Decimal contributions and HALF_UP displays follow below. IAS uses 25% unrounded BQS, 35% R, 20% D, 10% P and 10% L. It has 35% coverage; its remaining 65% is missing, not redistributed. Its broad uncertainty interval is only an arithmetic diagnostic, not an investment score.

No governance cap is invoked because GOV is above 3 and no G1 failure is evidenced. No funding-failure cap is invoked because the firm has no established current unfinanceable obligation; stressed model failures are not defaults. The persistent weak-CAP/CASH GQS ceiling was explicitly assessed and does not apply: both factors are 6, supported by positive multi-year cash conversion and a reconciled earlier reinvestment record. The gate exclusion still prevents a favorable investment classification and all cross-company ranking.

Material factor sensitivities are transparent: CAP 5–7 changes BQS by±0.12 and GQS by±0.15; MOAT 4–6 changes BQS by±0.20; REV 7–8 allows deterioration but no unsupported upgrade. These are not discretionary hidden haircuts after the formula.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
Mobilise sells and implements ERP-oriented software to institutional and enterprise buyers. HRevO handles payroll and human-resource workflows; OpsSuite covers maintenance, assets and facilities; SCMPro covers procurement/supply-chain processes; EduPro handles school administration. FY2025 product revenue was ₹8.5213 crore HRevO, ₹4.7973 crore OpsSuite, ₹2.1947 crore SCMPro and ₹0.6276 crore EduPro. HRevO supplied 52.79% of revenue, not all of it.

The pricing units matter. HRevO combines active-employee/month licensing with annual or multi-year enterprise lump sums. EduPro charges per student/month. OpsSuite can charge per asset, per site or an enterprise package. SCMPro is normally priced for the full project scope. Monthly recurring charges fund access/support/updates, but change requests, customization, implementation and project work also generate revenue. A software licence accepted upon delivery is not automatically a ratable subscription.

Software-service revenue is recognized as services are rendered, while licensing can be recognized on shipment and acceptance when obligations and collection conditions are satisfied. Cash therefore depends on invoices, acceptance and credit terms, not merely on counting installed users. The latest report recognizes one segment and the July response describes India as the geographic reporting segment; deployments at customers elsewhere in Asia are not proof of material direct exports. The AR’s foreign-exchange earnings are only ₹0.63 lakh.

No recurring/nonrecurring revenue split, ARR bridge, gross/net retention cohort or customer acquisition payback was found. Repeat-customer revenue is a useful relationship indicator but includes repeat projects and does not measure contracted future cash. The manpower-related MobiliseIE interest is analyzed separately; no additional partnership revenue, profit or enterprise value is silently consolidated into the issuer model.

sections.title: Moat and Industry Position
sections.text:
The plausible advantage is switching friction: payroll rules, employee records, asset histories and integrated workflow customizations take effort to migrate. The observed evidence is repeat business and a multi-product relationship with large customers. Durability depends on continued product quality, integrations, service response and the customer’s willingness to retain the platform. The failure mode is equally clear: a dominant enterprise customer can rebid, internalize or replace the system, negotiate pricing, or shrink employee/site counts.

The largest customer supplied 75.07% of FY2025 revenue and 57.78% in 9M FY2026; the top 10 provided 97.39% and 94.08%, respectively. Lower concentration in the interim is encouraging but not yet proof of independently diversified demand. With one buyer so important, company switching costs and customer bargaining power coexist. Customer logos and implementation experience cannot by themselves establish pricing power.

Microsoft Azure hosting and reported ISO/CMMI/security capability support delivery reliability; they do not create an exclusive technology asset. Planned AI/GPU functionality is investment intention, not monetization evidence. No verified market-share denominator or network-effect mechanism was found. An analyst should not compare the entire Indian IT market with Mobilise’s sales and call the difference an addressable opportunity.

The comparative set is used for business questions, not for borrowing a valuation. Unicommerce’s subscription/usage commerce software has measurable client/transaction disclosures but FY2025 first-time consolidation after Shipway changes scope. IRIS has regulatory reporting software and disclosed ARR, not the same HR/ERP mix. Ramco supplies enterprise/payroll products at a different global scale and accounting basis. Their greater disclosure of recurring economics highlights what Mobilise must establish; none is a clean multiple match.

sections.title: Revenue Growth and Scale
sections.text:
Six reported annual revenue observations are available: FY2021 ₹2.2750 crore, FY2022 ₹3.5603 crore, FY2023 ₹6.9451 crore, FY2024 ₹12.0560 crore, FY2025 ₹16.1409 crore and FY2026 ₹18.4297 crore. They span LLP accounts, IPO restatements and the latest statutory presentation. The five-year reported CAGR is 51.95%; the three-year FY2023–26 diagnostic is 38.45%; the two-year internally consistent IPO-restated FY2023–25 CAGR is 52.45%. A ten-year CAGR is unavailable, not zero.

REV uses the three-year software-revenue history rather than pretending the older LLP tax/depreciation framework is identical. The statutory FY2025 comparison is ₹16.18 crore, only ₹0.0391 crore above the restated revenue. That difference does not erase real scaling, but it must not be hidden. Annual additions through the mixed series are ₹1.2853, ₹3.3848, ₹5.1109, ₹4.0849 and ₹2.2888 crore; the latest same-basis addition is ₹2.2497 crore.

The latest trajectory is slower: statutory FY2026 growth 13.90%; H1 growth 27.30% and H2 growth 4.49%; Q4 sales declined 4.08%. The two halves, not just one weak quarter, justify a net−1 trajectory adjustment from the>=30% CAGR starting score 9. The resulting 8 also respects the medium-confidence/history ceiling. Small scale is not an extra penalty.

The driver evidence is product mix: HRevO grew strongly into FY2025, OpsSuite broadened, while EduPro fell between FY2023 and FY2025 before improving in 9M FY2026. No reliable decomposition into price, user counts, customer additions and implementation revenue is available. The July 2025 partnership acquisition is a related manpower interest rather than evidence of material externally acquired issuer software sales. Organic continuity is plausible, not certified. No post-March quarterly revenue is invented or annualized into TTM.

sections.title: Growth Quality and Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
The company can grow through more payroll users, additional assets/sites, cross-selling and new institutional customers. The IPO specifies 36 new technical hires, marketing expansion and infrastructure investment, which identifies concrete resources rather than only a headline TAM. It does not disclose customer-level conversion probabilities, acquisition costs or attributable returns for those hires.

The strongest economic evidence is the coherent FY2023–25 restated investment bridge. IC rises ₹1.4175 to ₹5.1318 crore and normalized NOPAT ₹1.6902 to ₹4.6534 crore. The ₹3.7143 crore capital increase reconciles to ₹4.8847 crore cash capex less ₹0.9880 crore D&A plus ₹−0.1823 crore ONWC movement, within ₹0.0001 crore rounding. The 79.78% incremental proxy comfortably exceeds a reasoned 14–20% nominal INR capital-cost range. That is evidence of genuine capital efficiency, not a penalty for lacking private project cohorts.

It is only a two-year window, however. Existing-customer expansion, better utilization and accounting restatement also contribute; the ratio is not the IRR of new software releases. The latest statutory FY2026 opening uses a different software basis, preventing a defensible three/five-year current capital comparison. Fully expensed development EBIT falls to ₹2.2662 crore from the FY2025 restated ₹4.2802 crore; even excluding ₹0.7 crore robotics it is ₹2.9662 crore. The business is not automatically cash-light simply because its physical assets are small.

GQS 6.45 acknowledges strong demonstrated revenue expansion while tempering duration, capital attribution and recurring per-share earnings. The upside requires the expensive new delivery capacity to create durable revenue faster than payroll/cloud costs. The program’s budget ends in June 2027; its recurring staffing, marketing and service costs do not end then.

sections.title: Management, Governance and Execution
sections.text:
The promoter group expected to retain 70.65% after the IPO, based on 6.72 million shares in the prospectus. At 31 March 2026 the annual report separately lists 6.58 million shares held by the three named promoters; this is not the same as the broader promoter-group definition. A secondary 70.68% group figure was not promoted into an independently verified cutoff fact. The prospectus reported no promoter pledge at its date; a current cutoff pledge assertion is not made without the later primary pattern.

Director remuneration was ₹1.32 crore versus ₹1.80 crore previously, or 23.60% of FY2026 PAT; director rent ₹0.186 crore and related manpower payments ₹0.36 crore are additional. The ₹0.7031 crore guarantee covers director borrowing at HDFC and declined from ₹1.0118 crore. It creates minority exposure without constituting immediate company debt. CARO’s aggregated guarantee/loan wording is reconciled to the contingent-liability note, not counted twice.

The complete FY2026 audit is unmodified, IFC adequate/effective, audit trail operating and CARO reports no default or fraud. FY2025 audit-trail software was absent, and the earlier lack of internal audit was stated not to be a statutory requirement then. Those are specific dated facts: remediation deserves recognition, while a clean headline opinion alone does not establish flawless stewardship.

The July 3 response, announced July 16, fixed XBRL share-capital denomination and omitted diluted EPS and improved readability. It explicitly retained the earlier financial contents. The later annual report reclassified IPO premium out of CFO, which is a meaningful correction. It still prints a share-capital-change line containing the noncash bonus, although cash-only arithmetic reconstructs the stated financing total.

MobiliseIE is described as 98% subsidiary, promoter partnership and an acquired associate across documents, while the directors’ report says no subsidiary/associate/JV. The amount is small but the economic ownership, remaining consideration and profit attribution need an answer. March IPO object spending was zero against plan ₹1.2075 crore, but the issue closed only at February-end and the monitor reports no deviation; that observation is a timing watchpoint, not a proven operational failure.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
Three accounting tracks are preserved rather than spliced. The FY2021/22 LLP scans show revenue and reported profit before unprovided tax; these profits are not presented as corporate PAT. The prospectus contains FY2023–25 restated statements and explains revenue timing, software salary/server capitalization, depreciation and tax adjustments. FY2026 statutory accounts refer back to older FY2025 statutory figures. The historic software change is therefore not invented fraud, but its carry-forward into the current period needs reconciliation.

The material FY2025 differences are equity ₹1.1086 crore and software ₹1.0817 crore. The latter equals 19.34% of FY2026 PAT and 3.63% of current equity. A purported ₹0.7296 crore cash discrepancy mostly disappears when ₹0.7042 crore noncurrent bank deposits are included, leaving ₹0.0254 crore. This distinction matters: a classification difference should not become an allegation of missing money.

FY2026 PBT ₹7.5187 crore includes ₹0.3804 crore other income and ₹0.2668 crore prior-period income. Removing both and adding ₹0.008 crore financing gives operating EBIT ₹6.8795 crore, EBITDA ₹8.2220 crore and normalized operating PAT ₹5.1421 crore at 25.168% tax. Balance writebacks contribute ₹0.2579 crore within other income. Credit-loss writeoffs in operating expenses are not casually added back. Software additions ₹4.9272 crore plus robotics ₹0.7 crore far exceed ₹1.0139 crore software amortization. Expensing all development leaves ₹2.2662 crore economic EBIT; this is a conservative lens, not a claim that capitalization under AS26 is intrinsically improper.

The annual report CFO bridge is PBT 7.5187+D&A 1.3425+finance 0.008−dividend 0.0012−interest 0.1195+gratuity 0.3237=9.0722 before working capital. Receivables−0.2880, payables−1.1343, inventory−0.0214, other CL−2.3347, advances−0.0798 and other CA+0.0467 leave ₹5.2608 crore. The other CL cash-flow line exceeds the balance-sheet decline by ₹1.2978 crore; current tax less tax payable less audit-provision increase explains ₹1.2977 crore. Taxes appear embedded, so subtracting another tax charge would double count. A clearer issuer cash-tax statement would still improve confidence.

CFO less ₹6.0446 crore operating capex is ₹−0.7838 crore. Before correction, the original filing put ₹14.5288 crore net IPO premium in operations; the annual report moves it to financing and leaves total cash unchanged. The cashflow’s ₹5 crore noncash bonus is removed analytically from the printed capital movement. No second IPO receipt is created.

Trade receivables ₹4.2636 crore are almost entirely under six months, versus ₹3.9756 crore in the prior statutory year. Average-receivable days are about 81.6 using revenue as a credit-sales proxy; a low inventory/payables cycle computed on mismatched software cost categories would be misleading. Related-party guarantee, gratuity ₹0.3237 crore, tax payable ₹0.6189 crore, IPO costs and unpresented cheques are treated once. All operating software is within EV; no separate property/software resale value is added to earnings value.

sections.title: Valuation and Market Expectations
sections.text:
The dated market cap is ₹96.7846 crore, with 9.512 million shares. Reported FY2026 EPS on current shares is ₹5.8791; this differs from weighted-average EPS in filings and should not be mistaken for historical diluted EPS. The IPO expanded bonus-adjusted preissue shares from 7 million to 9.512 million, 35.89% more shares and 26.41% ownership dilution for a nonparticipating preissue holder. The earlier bonus itself is not economic dilution.

At March 2026, ₹17.13 crore of ₹19.3807 crore cash was earmarked. Simple EV netting all IPO cash would overstate freely distributable surplus. Using only unearmarked cash gives approximately ₹94.6247 crore EV before operating-reserve refinements, or 11.51 x reported operating EBITDA. That EBITDA excludes cash software reinvestment and is not the valuation base in the forecast.

The cash-cost model runs monthly from 1 April 2026 to 20 October 2031, explicitly splitting the 20 October 2026 entry. It pays old tax, gratuity, debt and issued-cheque settlements once; keeps restricted cash separate; releases it only against eligible spend; carries unfinished FY2026 budget into the first FY2027 quarter; and retains recurrent staff/marketing/cloud costs beyond June 2027. Overlap between announced program costs and baseline expenses is assumed 50% in base, 0% bear and 70% bull, not represented as a disclosed fact. Ordinary software development is expensed economically; a separate capitalization/amortization proxy prevents pretending this immediately removes cash taxes.

FY2026 cash EBITDA after all development is about 14.08% of sales; excluding the disclosed robotics project from repeat development gives about 17.88%. The base 18% starting core margin therefore assumes that project is not repeated at the same intensity, while the bull 22% requires further operating improvement. These are analyst assumptions, not guidance.

Base:18% growth, 18 to 22% core cash EBITDA margin before incremental program costs, 65 ONWC days, 2.5% sales maintenance tangible capex and 14 x terminal economic EBIT. Terminal TTM revenue ₹46.29 crore, EBIT ₹4.03 crore, EV ₹56.39 crore, net equity ₹60.64 crore and algebraic ₹63.75/share. Its conditional IRR is-8.93%. Conditional entry values at 12/15/18% are ₹36.18/ ₹31.70/ ₹27.87; none is an authorized buy price while G2 is open.

Bull:30% growth, 22 to 28% core margin, 50 days, 70% overlap and 20 x economic EBIT produces 31.08%. It requires materially better scale and economics, not just a higher multiple. Sensitivities include growth×multiple and ONWC days×program-overlap grids, tax amortization, capex, guarantee, cash reserves and customer loss. Base 95 days or 0% overlap breaches funding and has no non-rescue return.

The reverse model verifies a finite funded crossing at 34.08% annual growth under the base margin/cost/multiple structure, with terminal revenue ₹94.76 crore. Both sides of the final narrow bracket are funded and residual is near zero. This is considerably above latest 13.90% growth. It is a conditional expectation test, not an inferred market consensus; a coarse search endpoint is not substituted for the root.

sections.title: Bear Case and Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The primary failure path is losing or repricing the dominant customer while committed engineering and support costs persist. The largest disclosed 9M FY2026 customer share 57.78% is used as a separate severe loss sensitivity; the main bear uses 30% initial revenue loss, 5% subsequent growth, 110 ONWC days, zero budget overlap, 3.5% maintenance capex, lower margins, 8 x terminal EBIT and a director-guarantee call.

This linked case breaches the analyst-selected reserve in the pre-entry period. Its negative algebraic future cash is a funding requirement, not a prediction that a company can operate indefinitely with negative cash. The non-rescue IRR and all non-rescue hurdle entry prices remain null. Reserves of ₹0.5/ ₹0.75/ ₹1.5 crore are separately tested; a reserve breach is not the same as legal insolvency.

The explicit rescue branch prefunds each interval before spending, issuing whole shares at an assumed 30% discount to the observed price with 4% fees. Gross, fees, net cash, dates, share expansion and current-holder ownership dilution are recorded separately. It is a counterfactual, not evidence that such financing exists, could be placed, or occurred before entry. The terminal enterprise value is zero when economic EBIT is negative; book software is not added as a liquidation windfall.

Other loss mechanisms are development assets that do not produce durable monetization, customer acceptance/collection delays, a larger recurring cloud cost base than expected, and illiquidity that prevents an orderly exit. At 5% participation, one whole lot was supportable on only one of the eight observed rows within the last 20 scheduled sessions. The biggest day accounted for 51.32% of observed 20 session turnover. Missing rows are not assumed zero volume, but observed trading does not justify promising a quick 3 lot exit.

sections.title: Fivefold and Tenfold Feasibility
sections.text:
A fivefold share-price outcome over the exact five-year horizon requires roughly 38% annual price compounding; tenfold requires roughly 58.5%. That arithmetic is not a forecast. The model solves the necessary revenue growth while holding the base margin/cost/14× multiple structure and explicitly checking funding, not merely multiplying current EPS by a speculative future P/E.

The algebraic fivefold and tenfold roots require approximately 53.14% and 71.33% revenue CAGR, respectively. Both fail the dated funding test before entry, so required funded non-rescue growth is NS, not those root values. Full terminal revenue, EBIT, capital needs, cash shortages and a rescue counterfactual at each algebraic root are embedded in the model. Raising the shortfall dilutes shareholders and means the naive undiluted target is no longer reached at the same growth rate.

This is not evidence that the total software market is too small. The constraint is Mobilise’s demonstrated ability to acquire and retain enough independent customers, staff delivery, fund growth and keep economics after development costs. No verified niche market-size/market-share denominator allows a defensible required-share percentage. Larger-enterprise ERP vendors and niche suppliers make access contestable. The lower 10× multiple sensitivity further raises required operating performance, rather than assuming today’s multiple only expands.

The right milestone is not a 5× label today. It is sustained post-IPO software cash profit, concentration reduction, reconciled financials and a funded customer-acquisition engine. Without those, even a plausible broad industry growth story cannot establish a fivefold or tenfold per-share path.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
Prioritize the next half-year result and September IPO monitoring report, normally due after this research cutoff. Reconcile reported cash, actual object spend, new staff/product commercialization and ongoing cloud costs. Do not treat a monitoring report’s absence before its normal due date as a regulatory breach. 

Request a precise FY2025 restated-to-statutory opening bridge for software/equity, not a generic clean-opinion assurance. Reconcile MobiliseIE investment 15.40 lakh, unpaid 10.40 lakh, profit share 3.84 lakh and 98% interest to the FY2026 unquoted 5 lakh balance and contradictory perimeter wording. A coherent accounting explanation could resolve the hold without proving anyone acted improperly.

Operational triggers: two comparable halves of growth below 10%, largest customer still above 50% without contract protection, all-development-expensed EBIT remaining below FY2025 levels, or material receivables moving beyond 6 months would weaken the thesis. Stronger evidence would be recurring/nonrecurring splits, independently understandable renewal cohorts, product gross margins and customer additions beyond the dominant buyer.

Funding triggers: unrestricted cash after old obligations below the chosen reserve, ONWC near 95 days, or a fully incremental IPO expense base without offsetting gross profit require immediate remodelling. Watch director-guarantee exposure, related-party term changes and any new share claims. For market execution, refresh dated lot/series/band/surveillance and actual quotes; do not use an observed-only ADV as a guaranteed calendar exit schedule.

sections.title: Final Classification and Conditional Action
sections.text:
Final classification: Hold — unresolved. Not a validated compounder designation, not Avoid — governance, and not observed financial distress. BQS/GQS remain calculable diagnostics because genuine business and historical capital-efficiency evidence exists; all ranking eligibility is nevertheless withheld because the current economic measurement basis is central to the thesis.

A new purchase cannot be justified by the headline 17 x earnings multiple alone. Clear the G2 bridge, establish recurring software economics after development and continuing IPO-funded costs, then rerun funded returns at an executable price. A lower quote does not itself resolve unreliable inputs. Conversely, a credible accounting explanation and demonstrated cash profit would warrant reassessment rather than preserving a hold mechanically.

For an existing holder, the appropriate next decision depends on position size, tax cost, liquidity and tolerance for customer concentration; none was supplied. The analysis therefore gives research conditions, not a personalized sell order. The ₹500000 case is solely an implementation benchmark:3 lots fit under budget; 4 lots do not. Limit-order availability and actual market depth need checking before any action.

The independent countercase is explicit: low debt, previous positive FCF, successful product scaling and a funded bull case are strengths. The bearish countercase is also explicit: capitalized development, concentrated customers and recurrent cost commitments can make an apparent cash-rich software company a poor per-share investment.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions and Open Questions
sections.text:
Source priority is original company/exchange documents, then analyst arithmetic. Secondary pages were used only to discover official filings; their cashflow and EPS values were not accepted without reconciliation. Sources include complete FY2026 and FY2025 annual reports, final prospectus, July clarification, monitoring report, historical LLP scans and exact-dated NSE market payloads. Source URLs, SHA256 hashes, page locators and evidence IDs are retained in the registers.

The report distinguishes disclosed facts, calculated ratios, management claims, analyst assumptions and absences of disclosure. Major unresolved inputs are the current software opening bridge, economic partnership ownership, exact recurring revenues, program overlap and September deployment. The latest full FY is March 2026; the pre-entry April–October cash bridge is a scenario, not an audited October bank balance. The independent tax-capitalization proxy and maintenance-capex range are assumptions, not company guidance or tax advice.

Software asset amortization, current tax, existing liabilities, IPO expenses, contingent guarantees and share issuance are separately reconciled to avoid double counting. No missing cashflow is replaced by PAT; no absent market row is made into a zero trade; no noncash bonus becomes financing; no unfinanced case receives an ordinary return or bargain entry price. Forecast confidence is constrained accordingly.

Private source-safe backup packages contain the complete analytical inputs, reports, models and validation code, not original shareholder lists, personal tax identifiers, raw PDF/OCR/images or transfer credentials. Deterministic reproduction validates arithmetic and consistency, not original-source authenticity. Research is not personal investment advice and the heuristic scores are not a validated return-prediction system.

Conditional base model pays all development cash, continues program costs after June 2027, keeps restricted IPO balances separate and tax-capitalization lag. Growth 18%, core margin 18 to 22%, 65 ONWC days and 14 x terminal economic EBIT give a funded but unattractive conditional return.

Customer-loss, 95 ONWC days or zero program-cost overlap can break the cash floor. The full 30% loss/110 days/zero-overlap bear has a pre-entry breach; non-rescue return is null. Neither an assumed cash reserve nor a modeled future shortfall is an observed default.

No contract-level ARR, GRR, NRR, CAC/LTV or reliable market-share denominator found. Long-lived customer relationships and certifications are evidence of capability, not a network effect or proven pricing power.

restrictions: No acquisition profit or investment value included in operating EV: standalone issuer economics only.
No new equity/debt in ordinary cases; all rescues explicitly counterfactual.
No IPO deposit is added to free equity value without future eligible spending and required operating reserve.
Program overlap is a sensitivity, not a disclosed fact; eligible underlying spending is counted once in modeled core costs and IPO costs are not double deducted.
Talent, marketing and infrastructure service costs recur after June 2027; GCP is a finite contingency budget, not a recurring commercial cost.
Monthly cash-floor test uses start-of-period funding for counterfactual rescues; intramonth daily bank balances are unavailable.

Cash taxes do not assume that economically expensing development creates an immediate tax deduction. A separate conservative software capitalization/amortization proxy feeds taxable earnings; this is an analyst tax-basis assumption, not company tax advice.

assumptions_and_limits: No acquisition profit or investment value included in operating EV: standalone issuer economics only.
No new equity/debt in ordinary cases; all rescues explicitly counterfactual.
No IPO deposit is added to free equity value without future eligible spending and required operating reserve.
Program overlap is a sensitivity, not a disclosed fact; eligible underlying spending is counted once in modeled core costs and IPO costs are not double deducted.
Talent, marketing and infrastructure service costs recur after June 2027; GCP is a finite contingency budget, not a recurring commercial cost.
Monthly cash-floor test uses start-of-period funding for counterfactual rescues; intramonth daily bank balances are unavailable.

Cash taxes do not assume that economically expensing development creates an immediate tax deduction. A separate conservative software capitalization/amortization proxy feeds taxable earnings; this is an analyst tax-basis assumption, not company tax advice.
No current live price replaces the dated reference, and no post-cutoff operating result is inferred.
Historical market coverage is incomplete. Missing issuer rows are not zero-volume observations.
Model prices and returns are conditional cases, not ordinary ratings or recommendations.
summary:
Hold — unresolved. Mobilise App Lab is a real, profitable enterprise-software and services business, not merely a technology label. Its earlier cash generation and capital efficiency deserve credit. The current evidence nevertheless does not establish a durable, broadly diversified subscription compounder, and the quoted valuation is less inexpensive after charging software development and preserving the IPO spending commitments.

Business Quality is 5.5 /10 (unrounded 5.46); Growth Quality is 6.5 (unrounded 6.45); Investment Attractiveness is NS. All ranking eligibility is withheld while the material financial-basis bridge remains unresolved. This is a research hold, not an allegation of fraud or an observed funding default.

At the verified 19 October 2026 close of ₹101.75, market capitalization is ₹96.7846 crore. The approximately 17.31 x reported earnings multiple rises to 18.82 x normalized operating earnings and roughly 57.07 x the deliberately conservative fully-expensed-development NOPAT proxy. These are different earnings lenses, not interchangeable peer P/Es. The funded base cash-cost case returns -8.93% annually over the exact October 2026–October 2031 horizon, while the bull reaches 31.08%. The bear is not financeable under its assumptions and has no non-rescue return. Do not average these into a target.

The decisive questions are customer concentration, how much development is genuinely growth investment versus maintenance, and whether the IPO-funded staffing/cloud budget creates incremental recurring profit. No purchase or sale is being proposed.
